memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then they are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the
doorframes of the houses where they eat the lambs." - Ex 12:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The lamb's death was not enough by itself. The blood had to be applied.

Think carefully about that. Every Israelite family had access to the same
instruction, the same lambs, the same night. But the blood on the doorframe was
what made the difference. A family could have killed a lamb, cooked it, eaten
it, and still have lost their firstborn if the blood stayed in the basin.

This is one of the clearest pictures of the Gospel in the Old Testament. Christ
died once for all, and His blood is fully sufficient. But Scripture is equally
clear that it must be personally received. Paul speaks of "faith in his blood"
(Rom 3:25). John writes that "to all who did receive him, to those who believed
in his name, he gave the right to become children of God" (John 1:12).

Nobody is saved by proximity to the truth. Being near a church, raised in a
Christian family, familiar with the words, none of that is the blood on the
door.

The question that night was never "Do you know about the lamb?" It was "Is the
blood on your door?"

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you personally trusted Christ, or only lived near Christian things?
2. What is stopping you from settling this today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, I do not want to merely know about You. I trust in Your blood shed
for me, and I ask You to be my Saviour. Amen.
